One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

draft_copy.headline: ROOM ABOVE TWO HUNDRED
draft_copy.deck: The week the pressure reached everyone
draft_copy.body: By Sunday night, the Commonwealth had learned that a number could become a weapon without anyone lifting a blade. Two teams had crossed two hundred. One sent a hamburger to a birthday party; another brought an army to a mountain gate. A centaur was chasing an outlaw through Highland mud. In the eastern ruins, a river quietly made a mockery of Red Leopards’ sandbags, while a second gust carried the same storm's reach to a court farther inland. Seven Deadly Chins found the one household that needed quiet and arrived with a jackhammer. Slob on my Dobb made a beer delivery through a swamp whose owner could no longer command the road. The front belonged to El Niño; the humiliations belonged to the men who chose them. With four regular-season games now remaining, the question was no longer simply who won. It was what each result would leave behind.

publication_copy.deck: The week the pressure reached everyone
publication_copy.body: By Sunday night, the Commonwealth had learned that a number could become a weapon without anyone lifting a blade. Two teams had crossed two hundred. One sent a hamburger to a birthday party; another brought an army to a mountain gate. A centaur was chasing an outlaw through Highland mud. In the eastern ruins, a river quietly made a mockery of Red Leopards’ sandbags, while a second gust carried the same storm's reach to a court farther inland. Seven Deadly Chins found the one household that needed quiet and arrived with a jackhammer. Slob on my Dobb made a beer delivery through a swamp whose owner could no longer command the road. The front belonged to El Niño; the humiliations belonged to the men who chose them. With four regular-season games now remaining, the question was no longer simply who won. It was what each result would leave behind.

draft_copy.headline: KEEP THE WHOLE LEAGUE IN VIEW
draft_copy.deck: Commissioner’s note • After Week 10
draft_copy.body: There is a difference between being beaten and having to live with the evidence. A score is entered once. A birthday photograph is shown forever. A broken hoop stays broken until someone fixes it. The owner of a swamp still has to watch the next truck drive through. That is the Commonwealth we have spent seasons building, and it is why this league is more than six boxes on a scoreboard. But our stories do not outrank the standings. Nobody is going to Cancún by mathematical decree until the last route is closed. Nobody is healed because a reserve slot looks full. The numbers have settled, and six teams now share 6–4 records. The next week will ask each of us what we have left to field.

publication_copy.deck: Commissioner’s note • After Week 10
publication_copy.body: There is a difference between being beaten and having to live with the evidence. A score is entered once. A birthday photograph is shown forever. A broken hoop stays broken until someone fixes it. The owner of a swamp still has to watch the next truck drive through. That is the Commonwealth we have spent seasons building, and it is why this league is more than six boxes on a scoreboard. But our stories do not outrank the standings. Nobody is going to Cancún by mathematical decree until the last route is closed. Nobody is healed because a reserve slot looks full. The numbers have settled, and six teams now share 6–4 records. The next week will ask each of us what we have left to field.

pages.candidate_render_prompt:
One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

illustrated_page_brief.artist_prompt:
One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

pages.text_image_integration:
Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

holding.title: No Private Exit
holding.copy: D0nkey K0ng finished the binding in the middle of the ring. Chili lay hogtied in the storm mud, sunglasses crooked, his decorated hat just beyond reach. Laughter rolled down from the galleries. The outlaw who had made a champion the joke last week could now see every person enjoying this one.
holding.visual: A low, wider public aftermath shows Chili hogtied in mud at the ring’s center. DK has stopped, braced all four legs and deliberately finished the binding; hand placement and the already caught rope explain the transition. This is humiliating slapstick, not injury spectacle. Chili’s face is readable and clear of the mud. The visible crowd laughs, points and reacts from safe rails. No main cast is teleported in as spectators. A dropped hat at arm’s reach, readable outlaw belt and the expansive empty space between Chili and the gate make the humiliation personal. The shot retains enough of the stands to prove it happened in front of everyone.

unresolved.title: The Encounter Remains Open
unresolved.copy: Chili cut toward the gate. The centaur’s loop arrived first. A boot skated through the churned mud, the rope drew tight, and the outlaw’s grand escape became the part everyone would remember. D0nkey K0ng stopped with four hooves planted. There was still work to finish, and the crowd had an excellent view.

illustrated_page_brief.artist_prompt:
One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

pages.title: One More Bag
pages.narrative_job: Red tries to save his damaged soccer pitch, then revisits the remembered Central Basin court and watches its wall-mounted hoop fail under a falling limb.

draft_copy.headline: One More Bag
draft_copy.deck: Red Leopards vs El Niño
draft_copy.body: The river did not arrive as a wall. It climbed a little, found a gap, and waited for Red Leopards to believe the last sandbag had solved it. The old goal leaned over a pitch still carrying last week's damage. Red Leopards shifted another bag into place. The water went around it. In 2022, he had beaten El Niño twice and carried thirteen wins into the semifinal. It was not the strength of the old season he remembered now, but how little of it had mattered on the night it ended.

draft_copy.deck: Red Leopards vs El Niño
draft_copy.body: Later, in the Central Basin, Red Leopards reaches the old basketball court, a place associated with a different recent victory. The same expanding front has arrived by a different road. A gust twists the branches above the familiar rim. He has barely looked up when the old limb comes down across the backboard. One storm, two places, and no time to make either one safe.

Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

draft_copy.deck: Red Leopards vs El Niño
draft_copy.body: The hoop hangs wrong. Red Leopards sits beneath it with the mud of his failed sandbag line still on him. El Niño laughs across the rain-swept court, and the 2022 semifinal comes back in full: 116.32 to 97.96, a 13–1 favorite sent home, and El Niño eventually lifting that season's title. Red Leopards is not eliminated today. That is almost the cruelest part. He still has to decide whether to get up and repair another thing.

holding.copy: The branch settled against the wall. The rim hung bent beneath it. Red sat at the court’s edge with nothing left in his hands. Across the stone, El Niño laughed into the wind. “You remember 2022.” Red did. Thirteen wins had not saved that season. Watching the broken hoop, he could feel that old uncertainty arriving again.

illustrated_page_brief.artist_prompt:
One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.

- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

illustrated_page_brief.artist_prompt:
One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

pages.candidate_render_prompt:
One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

holding.copy: His Majesty’s Blood pressed the cake into Duckhook’s face before the birthday boy found his speech. Frosting spread across white feathers and orange bill as the dining hall erupted around them. The champion’s belt caught the warm light beside the open present. The 200 Burger remained magnificent. reversal.title: The Birthday Belongs to Its Host
reversal.copy: Duckhook watched the champion reach for the cake and moved first. The elaborate gift stayed open on the table while the birthday boy redirected the prank toward its author. His guests finally found the applause he had been expecting. The burger was still enormous. The celebration belonged to its host again.

Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

holding.title: Unlimited Firepower
holding.copy: The second counterattack vanished beneath converging red fire. ObiWan Jacoby drove his green blade through the nearest burst and held the inner arch as the mountain approach disappeared in smoke. Across the wrecked causeway, The LLC lowered his hand. The surviving battery answered anyway. The difference between them was no longer a fraction on a ledger. It was how much fire remained after both of ObiWan’s answers.
holding.visual: The decisive image shows both counters attempted and contained. Obi yields the exposed approach under sustained fire while LLC controls the open ground; no invented death or permanent ownership transfer.

reversal.title: The Green Line Breaks Through
reversal.copy: ObiWan Jacoby used the first battery’s wreckage to draw the crossfire, then changed direction beneath the stone arch. His second assault reached the command platform before the surviving guns could turn. The LLC stepped back as the green blade cut through the firing controls. Across the causeway, the advancing formation stopped receiving its orders, and the Jedi kept moving.
reversal.visual: Resolve the same established props and battlefield through the described counter. No new unintroduced mechanism.

unresolved.title: The Encounter Remains Open
unresolved.copy: Red fire crossed the causeway while ObiWan Jacoby held his green blade toward the command platform. One battery burned behind him; the second counterattack had reached the ridge but not the commander. The LLC lifted a hand toward the surviving guns. Between those two movements, the entire mountain approach remained an unfinished blaze.
unresolved.visual: Hold the established encounter before its decisive action; no winning tableau.

tie.title: Neither Side Gives
tie.copy: The last battery fell silent as ObiWan Jacoby reached the broken edge of the command approach. The LLC held the far platform, and the green blade held the inner arch, with neither able to cross the smoking gap. Both counterattacks had been spent. Both lines still stood. The mountain carried the marks of a battle neither side could finish.

Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.

- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.

- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

One individual 1080×1920 grayscale integrated illustrated memo folio: complete supplied headline, department heading, deck, narration and source-qualified lettering in the exact intended final composition. No annotation cards, miniature scene summaries, detached document exports, or generated six-up grids.

Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.

pages.text_image_integration:
Image authority is explicit: current_appearance_override controls current face and costume; approved_lineup_crop supplies canonical identity; published_memo_precedent supplies only its stated layout/geometry application and never replaces current character anatomy or current scores. Follow the actual published memo references: one continuous cinematic world, prominent editorial hierarchy, slender ornament where appropriate, full narrative typography inside deliberate atmospheric reading space, and scene-led differences between departments. Grayscale affects palette, not the amount of copy, character identity, panel proportions, camera or final-page geometry.

SCENE-LED DESIGN RULES
- One complete 1080x1920 portrait folio may contain multiple deliberate camera views. The current visual_storytelling shot contract controls the sequence; a complete artwork is not limited to one shot.
- Preserve published typographic identity and department recognition; vary placement and scale with scene function.
- No default header/image/bottom-paragraph stack; typography and image are composed together.
- Keep complete source copy; compose space around it rather than cutting words to fit.
- Long prose is editorial typography, not implausibly engraved on tiny props.
- Use short in-world lettering only where physically plausible. Exact names, data, scores and tables are deterministically typeset, straight and legible.
- Identical department_heading and deck are displayed once; source fields are not interpreted as a command to repeat the same matchup line twice.
- Characters and props may cross decoration but never essential letters or data.
- Test full native page at 390px phone width; reflow the page rather than shrink the copy below readable scale.
- Canonical identity, appearance overrides, established geometry and verified final sports facts take precedence over composition novelty.
- All new personal quotes, jokes, anecdotes and factual claims require source/Founder input; an AI suggestion is not accepted canon.

SEQUENTIAL VISUAL STORYTELLING
- One complete 1080x1920 folio is the output artifact, not a rule requiring one camera view. Multiple shots/POV areas within that folio are explicitly authorized working direction.
- Use a visual sequence only when the additional view reveals new information: intention, cause, response or consequence. Do not pad with duplicate crops of the same pose.
- Distinguish simultaneous opposing POV from chronological action. Temporal cuts must not read as cloned characters or objects in one continuous space.
- Each action folio has a dominant image; subsidiary views earn their space. Avoid identical grids, mandatory equal splits and three strips on every page.
- Canon and exact factual lettering outrank novelty. Use each character’s current reference assets in every shot, preserve morphology, costume, companions and named location geometry.
- Preserve full publication copy once and in source order. Distribute it deliberately through the visual reading path; no additional mandatory caption below each image, no extra invented dialogue.
- A quiet master image and a level documentary table are intentional storytelling choices. Do not panelize every supporting page or turn Opening Drive into six miniature matchup posters.
- Match meaningful objects, material states and weather between pages. Editorial visual echoes do not prove physical adjacency, contemporaneity or character travel.
- Inspect each native folio and 390px reading proof for POV legibility, coherent cause, readable text and exact score before visual acceptance. Tests verify instructions only, never artistic success.
The visual_storytelling shot plan defines all within-page views. Existing camera/foreground fields describe the anchor scene, not a ban on supplementary or opposing views. Do not copy old paragraph-strip placement from a precedent.
